prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove a chosen protein, from the original PROTAC concept to structure-guided design of ternary complexes

statement.case_for: I have moved from B058 to B011 as a single-part prize. The chemical principle is stated in physical terms: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex with a target and an E3 ligase, and the cooperativity of that complex is a measurable design variable that converts binding into elimination. The principle has been reproduced by many independent groups and across target classes, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned a concept into rational chemistry. That is a mechanism-level contribution and not only a drug-discovery claim. Four members already hold B011 first and every member lists it as an alternative, so on scientific grounds the committee has one candidate whose merit is not disputed, only its timing and credit.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, so the clinical consequence remains expected and not demonstrated, and the citation must rest on the chemistry alone. Credit is crowded under a three-person limit: Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper, and Handa, Ito and Gray from the molecular-glue strand, are all omitted by a Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli trio, and the omission has to be defended openly. My own B058 remains scientifically sound and mature, but I could not answer the chair's question of what Gray and Winkler discovered that Marcus, Hopfield, and Dutton and Moser did not, in a form narrow enough to survive a priority challenge.

responses.point: Linke asked me to define exactly what Gray and Winkler discovered that others did not, and said B058 would deserve a second look only if that were settled.
responses.response: I cannot settle it to the standard a citation requires. The experimental demonstration with ruthenium-modified proteins is real and mature, but the distance dependence and the pathway picture are shared with Dutton and Moser and with Beratan and Onuchic, none of whom is credited, and Marcus's 1992 prize already covers the theory. A narrow wording around experiment in proteins is possible, yet it invites exactly the priority dispute I would want to avoid. That is the reason I withdraw B058 as my preferred configuration while keeping it as an alternative.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa in the trio because the cereblon identification is the chemical-mechanistic anchor of the molecular-glue branch and explains thalidomide-class drugs.
responses.response: I take the cereblon discovery seriously as mechanism, and as a biochemist I find it the best-measured part of this field. But it is a separate achievement about how an existing drug acts, while the Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli line is about designing degraders. A single citation covering both would be vague and would still omit Ito and Gray. I would prefer a PROTAC-centred citation that does not claim to cover glues, leaving the cereblon and glue strand open for later recognition. I note that Chabes has said he would accept Ciulli in the third place on that basis, and I hope he does.

responses.point: Aqvist treats PROTACs as a new pharmacological principle with real consequences but warns that timing is arguably slightly early and credit crowded.
responses.response: I share both reservations, and in round 1 I asked that demonstrated chemistry be separated from expected clinical benefit. My answer is to word the citation around the ternary-complex mechanism and the capability to remove a chosen protein, with no claim of therapeutic success. On that footing the twenty-year record and wide reproduction make the prize defensible even if no approval exists by the announcement.

responses.point: Somfai argues that Buchwald and Hartwig have a clean two-person credit, thirty years of confirmation and daily use, and that C-N coupling differs mechanistically from the 2010 C-C coupling prize.
responses.response: His chemical answer to the 2010 overlap is fair, and the maturity and attribution are better than for B011. My difficulty is that the question for the committee is which achievement can carry five votes with a defensible citation, and C-N coupling has the thinnest opening support. I do not dismiss it, but I would place a new mechanism-level capability above a refinement of an already recognised catalytic concept, and I would ask Somfai whether he would accept B011 if B055 cannot reach five.

responses.point: Sparr prefers phase separation as a physical-chemical organising principle but concedes that in-cell evidence is partly indirect and that Pappu and Mittag are left out.
responses.response: Her concession is the point on which I stay where I was: the in vitro polymer physics is solid, but physiological generality is disputed and credit cannot be fitted into three names without cutting central contributors. She lists B011 as an alternative and I would invite her to consider it the safer principle to recognise now.

uncertainties: No expert report on degrader clinical outcomes is available to me, and I have not verified whether any degrader will be approved before the announcement.
Whether the committee will accept a PROTAC-only citation that leaves out Handa, Ito and Gray, or whether Chabes and others will insist on the glue strand.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the right third name, and whether the omission of Sakamoto and Kim can be defended.
If B011 stalls, I do not have a settled second choice between B058, with its unresolved priority overlap, and B008, where structure is mature but the N2 binding mechanism is not.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal-level conflict. I work on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes, which is scientifically close to B058 and B008 but not to B011, where I have no stake. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, who is not a candidate. My move away from B058 is not driven by any personal tie.
